nominal rigidity in the housing rent is high and that it depends on the turnover and the income status of the household.
the rate of the nominal rigidities is high in housing rents in Turkey between 2010 and 2011 and that the incidence of nominal rigidities is higher among the nonturnover housing units.

the stickiness in housing markets in Turkey, and we show that the incidence of nominal and real rigidity in rents is high and it depends on the turnover and the grid pricing status of the units.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in addition to the institutional factors, the frictions imposed on tenants by the housing market also play an important role in the nominal rigidity of housing rents in Turkey.
the incidence of nominal stickiness in housing rent is high in Turkey, but the incidence of turnover is low.
, on average and for the majority of the units, the stickiness in rents is associated with turnover status and grid pricing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of nominal rigid rents and turnover status is not random and that there are important differences across income groups.
, relative to other tenants, high-income households face a higher opportunity cost to move and they are also more likely to have a better bargaining power with their landlords.
the nominal rigidity is a major feature of housing rents in Turkey, and it is more likely to occur in the nonturnover housing units.
The main takeaway from our work is that
housing rents are sticky in Turkey.
the stickiness of housing rents is not only associated with the turnover status of housing units, but it is also related to the characteristics of the tenants.
the nominal rigidity and turnover status of housing units are not random and they are associated with a variety of economic, social and psychological factors.
